q: Under the b=1 conditional distribution Pr[a|b=1]=(2/N) sin^2(pi k0 a/N), what is a provably consistent estimator for k0 with success bounds matching the b=0/cos branch? The paper's stated argmax over sum sin(2 pi k a_i / N) has expectation zero for every k by odd-function/symmetry arguments.
basis: During Qiskit statevector sweeps for N=16, k0=5 the b=1/sin branch achieved only ~10% success at m=60 versus 100% for the b=0/cos branch. The paper's headline query bound still goes through by restart/branch-choice arguments but the specific sin post-processing in the Theorem-3 proof is not consistent as written.
next_steps: (i) Formalize argmax_k |sum_i sin(2 pi k a_i / N)|^2 as a hypothesis test with an explicit Hoeffding bound (or reduce via sin^2 = 1 - cos^2 back to the cos branch). (ii) Empirically sweep the fixed estimator against b=0/cos on the same joint distributions using our existing harness. (iii) Contact P. Hoyer or check the published Adv. Appl. Math. version (25:239, 2000) for an erratum.

q: What is the true optimal constant C in m >= C ln N for the Ettinger-Hoyer estimator? We observe empirical m*_{1 - 1/(2N)} of 4, 30, 45, 60 for N=4,8,16,32 versus the paper's stated ceiling ceil(64 ln N) = 89, 134, 178, 222.
basis: Hoeffding-derived constants are typically loose by 1-2 orders of magnitude, but the ~30x gap we observe is unusual and worth characterizing. All results are from real Qiskit statevector simulation (TV distance vs Lemma 4 = 1e-16).
next_steps: (i) Reimplement the oracle as a permutation of computational basis states (no explicit 2^{2n+1} x 2^{2n+1} matrix) to scale to N=64, 128, 256. (ii) Fit m* vs ln N; conjecture the tight constant. (iii) Attempt a matching Chernoff-style lower bound on the estimator using the exact variance of cos(2 pi k a/N) under Prob[Z=z] to see whether the paper's Hoeffding step is provably improvable.

q: Can the O(N) classical post-processing be replaced by a poly(log N) procedure at least for structured k0? Kuperberg's 2003 subexponential sieve improved this to 2^{O(sqrt(log N))}, but our small-N sweep runs the exhaustive argmax; the exponential-time gap identified by the paper remains open in general.
basis: The paper explicitly leaves the polynomial-time post-processing question open. Our replication confirms the estimator is well-defined and successful on small N but scales linearly in N per query batch, exactly as the paper describes.
next_steps: (i) Implement Kuperberg's sieve on top of our sample generator for N up to 64 and compare oracle count + wall time to our exhaustive argmax. (ii) Empirically explore whether structured k0 (small hamming weight, small algebraic order) admit faster estimators. (iii) Cross-check against Regev's 2004 dihedral-HSP <-> uSVP reduction to gauge which structural properties matter.

q: How sensitive is the observed query-complexity constant to the specific choice of gamma (coset-representative encoding)? We used one canonical labelling per instance; the theoretical marginals are proved choice-independent, but numerical conditioning and finite-shot sampling could differ.
basis: We tested only a single gamma per (N,k0). Total variation vs Lemma 4 was machine-precision small, so the *distribution* is unambiguously correct, but the empirical Monte-Carlo constants might vary if gamma is permuted.
next_steps: (i) Add a --gamma-seed CLI flag to the harness that randomly permutes coset labels while preserving the coset partition. (ii) Repeat the m* sweep for 10-20 random gammas per (N,k0) and report mean +/- SD of m*_2/3. (iii) Verify TV distance stays at 1e-16 as sanity check on the invariance claim.

q: What is the query complexity for non-power-of-two N (particularly prime N with fewer subgroups)? Our implementation uses an n-qubit Z_N register requiring N to be a power of two; the paper's result is stated for general N.
basis: Our sweep covers N in {4,8,16,32} only. Since prime N have fewer non-trivial subgroups of order 2 (exactly N reflection subgroups vs N+1 for even N), the estimator's effective search space differs, and the Hoeffding constant may tighten or loosen.
next_steps: (i) Implement a qudit-style DFT or block-encoded F_N for N in {3,5,7,11,13}. (ii) Rerun the harness on those instances. (iii) Compare m*_2/3 vs ln N scaling by prime vs highly composite N and report whether the paper's stated bound is prime-friendly.
